newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: SAfrica Safex happy with rand/dollar futures trade.
newsitem.headline: SAfrica Safex happy with rand/dollar futures trade.

text.p: The start of trade in South Africa's rand/dollar futures contracts was slow but was expected to pick up as the year progressed, South African Futures Exchange (Safex) chief executive officer Stuart Rees said.
"It was entirely as expected. We expected a sluggish start by virtue of the fact that the market is restricted to authorised dealers and non-resident clients of members of Safex," he said.
"But the product will evolve over time," he added.
Rees told Reuters 20 contracts, worth around $2 million dollars, had traded on the day and a price had been shown virtually all day on at least two contracts.
Banking group Nedbank Ltd and Rand Merchant Bank had been the first two parties to trade a contract.
Dealers said trade was limited because all eyes would be on the launch later on Wednesday of a competing dollar/rand product on the Chicago Mercantile Exchange.
"The one to look out for will be the CME this afternoon. They will have the 'gungho' speculators that we don't have."
Dealing in the currency futures is seen as a further sign in the gradual relaxation of exchange controls.
